Now I have a complete picture. Let me also check the running OpenVLA experiments on westd-38929 for progress.

Key findings so far:

### westd-41074 (4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 98GB)
| GPU | PID | Experiment | Runtime | Status |
|-----|-----|------------|---------|--------|

| 2 | 68539 | M96 training | 1d7h | RUNNING |
| 3 | 59671 | M64v6 training | 1h30m | RUNNING |

The π0.5 random k=0.7 seed42 experiment finished with a success rate of 77.2% across 386 out of 500 trials in about 83 minutes. Now checking the westd-38929 cluster where OpenVLA experiments are running with the l2norm k=0.7 configuration on GPU 0.

Looking at the GPU assignments, I'm seeing OpenVLA experiments across all four GPUs with different k values and the v2 variant, all running for about 3 hours and 20 minutes. But there's something odd here—GPU 2 shows a result of 44.4% for the random k=0.7 v2 experiment, yet the process is still marked as running. The result file timestamp from May 21 at 12:07 doesn't match when this PID started roughly 3 hours and 20 minutes ago around 15:30, so this appears to be a re-run of the same configuration or possibly a different experiment altogether.

Checking the actual command lines for each process, I can see they're all using the same evaluation script but with different pruning modes and k ratios—L2norm k=0.7, random k=0.3, random k=0.7, and L2norm k=0.5. The random k=0.7 experiment on GPU 2 is definitely a re-run since the earlier result already exists.

Looking at the completed results, I notice we have coverage across different k values for both pruning methods, with success rates ranging from 25% to 70.6%. The pattern suggests that higher k values (0.9, 0.95) perform better than lower ones, and L2norm pruning seems to outperform random pruning at similar k ratios. Looking at the GPU allocation across both machines—westd-27271 has the L2norm k=0.3 rerun taking over 2.5 hours on one Blackwell GPU while the other runs M32 training, and cqa1-33015 is running the X-VLA experiment on its first GPU.

Now I'm reviewing the completed π0.5 results showing the baseline achieved 98.2% success rate, with random k=0.7 dropping to 77.2% and random k=0.5 further declining to 69.4%.  The L2norm variants show more dramatic degradation, particularly at k=0.5 (33.4%) and k=0.3 (51.0%), which is odd since k=0.3 performs better than k=0.5 — that non-monotonic pattern is concerning. Looking at the OpenVLA results, the L2norm k=0.95 and k=0.9 both hit 70.6%, but then drop sharply to 39.2% at k=0.5 and 25.0% at k=0.3.

Now I'm seeing the Random variants with v2 versions — k=0.95 v2 at 69.2% and k=0.7 v2 at 44.4%. I need to finalize the audit report for the completed π0.5 random k=0.7 experiment and update the registry, then check the logs on the running experiments to estimate when they'll finish.
